title: Tajziya: a parser federation for the classical languages of the human corpus, organised by family
description: Tajziya is a federation of parsers for the classical languages of the human written corpus, organised by genealogical family and built on the dhancha spine. Its registry holds 79 language and stage nodes taken from the author's candidate language matrix, each keyed by stage, script and corpus and carrying the matrix's own status, with every conflict in that source recorded rather than resolved. Parsing proceeds through the Project ILM layers (phonology, script pivot, orthography, segmentation, morphology, syntax) with CoNLL-U as the common output. One node parses: a Classical Sanskrit vowel-sandhi segmenter, in Python and JavaScript kept behaviour-identical by test, which returns every admissible segmentation. Every other node is bound to its family's frame, which refuses by name and points to the package that would build it. Shared engines are derived from the data by phenomenon, separating script mechanisms, which recur across unrelated lineages, from language mechanisms. The matrix's elimination rule computes each node's status from recorded corpus coverage, treats translation as lossy rather than as recovery, and declines to certify a minimum while the corpus universe and loss function remain open. A third-party sutra compilation used by the Sanskrit node is not redistributed; its hash is pinned so that a lawful local copy can be verified.
